# nexus package remove

Remove packages

Removes installed packages with apt-get remove: names, each of which must be installed under exactly that name (otherwise 404 not-found, and no operation is created). By default the configuration files and the automatically installed dependencies stay; purge true runs apt-get purge, deleting the configuration files too, and also accepts a package left with only its configuration files; autoremove true also removes the automatically installed dependencies nothing needs any more. Packages that depend on a named one are removed with it. whatIf true simulates with apt-get -s, changes nothing, does not wait for other apt operations, and returns preview: the packages it would remove. Side effects: removes packages and runs their maintainer scripts as root, which can stop services; never prompts; never reboots. Long-running: answers 202 with an operation, queued in order behind any other apt operation, that first waits up to providers.apt.lockWait for another process's dpkg lock, then fails package-manager-busy; fails package-manager-broken when dpkg reports an interrupted state, which it never repairs; fails apt-failed, naming apt-get's exit status, when apt-get fails. The result lists the packages changed and apt-get's exit status.

## Usage

```
nexus package remove NAMES... [flags]
```

## Examples

```
  # Remove packages
  nexus package remove <name>...
  # The same, safe to retry
  nexus package remove <name>... --idempotency-key <key>
```

## Flags

```
      --autoremove               Also remove the automatically installed dependencies nothing needs any more. Default false keeps them.
      --filter stringArray       key=value, repeatable: print only objects whose dot path has this value; a repeated key matches any of its values
      --follow                   stream the operation's output to stderr while waiting
  -h, --help                     help for remove
      --idempotency-key string   Idempotency-Key header: a retry with the same key and input returns the original operation (at most 255 visible ASCII characters)
      --names stringArray        Installed packages to remove, at least one, each named exactly, optionally with :architecture. Repeatable.
      --no-wait                  print the operation as accepted and exit, without waiting for it to end
  -o, --output string            output format: table, json, jsonl, yaml (default table on a terminal, jsonl otherwise)
      --purge                    Also delete the packages' configuration files. Default false keeps them.
      --select strings           print only these dot paths of each object, comma-separated, such as name,properties.state; host and id are always kept
      --tag strings              target every configured host with this tag; comma-separated or repeated for any of several
      --timeout duration         stop waiting after this long, such as 90s or 5m, and exit 7; the operation is not canceled
      --what-if                  Simulate only: change nothing and return the packages that would be removed.
      --yes                      do not ask for confirmation; required to mutate without a terminal
```

## Global flags

```
      --host string   target hosts: configured names, comma-separated, or all (default: NEXUS_HOST, then the default host)
      --verbose       log each request and response status to stderr
```
